summary: The PR-122 no-promotion firewall is scientifically sound in the declared evidence: process, evidence, and scientific status remain orthogonal; scientific status is OPEN; claim release is false; correlated internal principals cannot promote science; MES and D2 authority remain blocked; and no native/family/posterior claim is created. Final closeout nevertheless fails because the publication freeze pins stale PR-122 closure, graph, receipt, and MES-scan hashes while asserting exact receipt consumption, and because the governing roadmap's PR-150 card still mandates PR4/NPIPE download and analysis despite the frozen complete-skip instruction.

steelman.no_promotion: The design is strong: the v2 spec openly records that it is a post-implementation amendment and cannot establish preregistration or RESCUED status; it caps the artifact at exploratory C1 governance mechanics; an immutable exact-scope authority snapshot separates author and adjudicator roles while marking both as correlated internal identities unable to promote science; the closure keeps mechanics PASS separate from scientific OPEN and claim_release_allowed=false; MES/D2 remain explicitly blocked pending PR-124; the publication freeze and semantic guard prohibit native, family, MIO-posterior, and statistical-validation promotion.
steelman.pr4_skip: The latest PR-122 spec gives the user-directed data boundary an explicit typed firewall: PR4 download is not started, all PR4 work is skipped, and download/intake/reduction/analysis are forbidden. The closure records commands_run=0 and no data work, while BLOCKERS.md bars any combined PR3+PR4 inference. This is the correct fail-closed posture and should supersede older planning text.

evidence: publication_claim_freeze.md:22 pins pr122_claim_closure_report.json to 7465abab..., but sha256sum returns acba9616....
publication_claim_freeze.md:25 pins pr122_mes_successor_scan.json to 2a2358f2..., but sha256sum returns 1d5f9379....
CONTEXT_PACK.md:70-71 identifies the current graph and release-receipt hashes as c82c686f... and 3766b160..., while publication_claim_freeze.md:24 and 27 pins 33913d83... and 0e81d6b7....
pr122_spec.yaml:229-231 and 410-422 requires exact consumer binding; lines 263-268 make stale/invalid integrity hidden by policy a decisive falsifier.
findings.consequence: The freeze is not a current exact consumer of the declared PR-122 fixed point. Expected BLOCKED scientific policy cannot launder stale integrity, so G-PR122-FINAL-CONSUMERS and PR-122 closeout must remain failed even though no scientific promotion occurred.
findings.required_resolution: After the current graph/closure/receipt/MES artifacts are final, rebuild the publication freeze through the source-only launcher, verify every pinned path/hash/receipt ID/version, and rerun its check mode. Do not manually update hashes.

findings.title: PR-150 roadmap card still mandates the forbidden PR4/NPIPE data lane
evidence: The frozen context and current spec require a complete zero-command PR4 skip.
The roadmap requires both PR3 and PR4 ensembles, a PR4 download, a PR4 size-probe decision, PR4 null analysis, and a combined C3 output; it explicitly says PR4 is mandatory, not optional.
findings.consequence: The current run can honestly report commands_run=0, but the repository's governing execution plan still contains an instruction that would violate user scope.
findings.required_resolution: Downscope/replan PR-150 before it becomes runnable, with an explicit supersession note and no inferred PR4 completion or PR3+PR4 result.

findings.title: Human claim ledger conflates canonical owner and contributor
evidence: pr122_spec.yaml:6-11 correctly records owner COMMON, contributor HTT, and implementation scopes common/htt.
CLAIM_LEDGER.md:9 instead records Owner as COMMON/HTT.
The roadmap at lines 110-112 requires one canonical owner and separate contributors/adjudicator/implementation scope.
findings.consequence: The ledger weakens the ownership boundary and makes automated or human interpretation of the PR-122 claim owner ambiguous.
findings.required_resolution: Record COMMON as the sole owner and HTT as contributor/subject scope in a separate field or caveat.

findings.title: Claim ledger publishes an unbound 195-test integration count
evidence: CLAIM_LEDGER.md:9 cites a 132-test authoritative receipt and a 195-test consumer integration count without a path/hash/selector/environment receipt for the latter.
pr122_claim_closure_report.json:325-608 binds only the 132 collected and 132 executed authoritative receipt.
findings.consequence: The additional count is not reproducibly attributable from the assignment-declared evidence and can drift independently of the content-addressed graph.
findings.required_resolution: Either bind the 195-test suite to an exact execution receipt with selector/environment hashes or remove the count and cite the reproducible check command without a manual number.

findings.title: Publication freeze labels roadmap C-levels as Tier without distinguishing canonical ClaimTier
evidence: publication_claim_freeze.md:3-8 gives the artifact canonical claim_tier diagnostic_only, while the table at lines 103-114 uses a column named Tier containing C1-C4 roadmap levels.
The roadmap at lines 66-76 explicitly says the C0-C6 ladder and canonical ClaimTier are not one ordered enum.
findings.consequence: Readers can mistake scientific level C2/C4 for canonical conditional/validated status even though caveats correctly downclaim the rows.
findings.required_resolution: Rename the table column to Scientific level and, where material, add a separate canonical ClaimTier column.
